title: To Kill a Mockingbird
description: A Pulitzer Prize-winning novel set in the American South during the 1930s, told from the perspective of young Scout Finch. The story centers on her father, lawyer Atticus Finch, who defends a wrongly accused Black man in a racially divided town. It remains a standard text for secondary and university literature studies.

title: The Shining
description: Stephen King's psychological horror masterpiece following Jack Torrance, an aspiring writer and recovering alcoholic who accepts an off-season caretaker job at the snowbound Overlook Hotel. As malevolent supernatural forces take hold, his young psychic son Danny senses growing peril. A classic work of modern supernatural horror.

description: A Pulitzer Prize-winning masterpiece set in antebellum Virginia chronicling the life of Henry Townsend, a black farmer and former slave who becomes a slaveholder himself. The novel explores the complex moral contradictions of power and human ownership in pre-Civil War America.

title: Frankenstein
description: The pioneering nineteenth-century work that established modern science fiction and gothic horror traditions. Victor Frankenstein animates an artificial creature who is subsequently abandoned and seeks understanding from a hostile society. The text raises enduring philosophical questions on scientific ethics and human isolation.

title: Jane Eyre
description: A landmark Victorian bildungsroman tracing the life of an orphaned governess who asserts her moral independence and self-worth. Jane faces hardship at Lowood school and dark family secrets while working at Thornfield Hall. A foundational classic of English feminist literature and dramatic storytelling.

title: Normal People
description: A contemporary coming-of-age study charting the complicated relationship between Connell and Marianne from school in western Ireland through Trinity College.
